SCHUNK spin-off adopts TACTILIA name for industrial robot hands

The business founded in January adopts the TACTILIA name, focusing on modular hands and customer application testing through SCHUNK CoLabs.

TACTILIA Robotics ↗18 November 2026English editorial summary
StoryImages 3

From spin-off to a new name

On November 18, SCHUNK Humanoid Robotics announced that it now operates as TACTILIA Robotics. The Munich business is led by CEO Markus Netzer. It was founded in January 2026, so this announcement concerns its new identity and commercial direction rather than the creation of the company.

Hands for different robot platforms

TACTILIA is developing modular hands that combine mechanics, sensors, actuators and software for picking and positioning objects in production and logistics. The intended platforms include humanoids, cobots and mobile manipulators. The company emphasizes integration and continuous operation, making the contact between hand and object central to the product.

Application testing remains essential

The independent business retains access to SCHUNK expertise and 15 CoLabs worldwide for customer testing and application development. The release does not specify pricing, delivery dates or numerical performance results. Factory users still need to evaluate the hand against their own parts, cycle times and process requirements.
